findings.why_it_matters: Measured: report([ScanResult(..., hits = [], population = 0, exempted = 1, ...)]) returns 0, and with exempted = 0 it returns 2. The same predicate `dead(r) = r.population == 0 && r.exempted == 0` is at base Scan.jl:457, so behaviour did not change in this window. What changed is the promise. Base said zero population is DEAD 'whatever else it did'; head licenses the exemption escape. The next sentence was kept: 'a scan that measured nothing yet hit something is a scan whose own counter is wrong'. A ledger-exempted hit is still a hit, so head now calls a scan with a demonstrably wrong counter 'accounted for' rather than DEAD. The contract was rewritten to fit the code instead of the reverse.

findings.description: The stated defect (the new test cites ext#4 of 2026-09-11-check-docs-02) is that the skip swallowed an open round of a DISABLED instrument. The fix requires every problem to be `:open`, so it also turns the `:committed` refusal from a skip into a failure. No test covers that case: the added assertions exercise only :open plus :disabled. The base contracts disagree about which behaviour was promised. Base docs_build_skipped said a skip happens "when the gate refused with exit `1` and `GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP` is unset", which was the old behaviour. Base gate_or_skip said "only because a round of a docs instrument is open", which reads toward the new one. The new DocLints docstring was rewritten in the same hunk to state the widened rule: "or a round whose fixes were committed without it, fails the build". The change may be the intended reading, but it goes beyond the defect cited, it changes the exit of a previously green local build, and no test shows it was considered.

findings.why_it_matters: Concrete input: a working tree with no `CI` variable and an open check-docs round, in the state this repo was in between 47db044 (fix pass 1 committed, so HEAD moved past ROUND.head) and f4f99cd (the pass-1 verdict files under .gbg/rounds/<id>/verdicts/pass-1/ were still untracked). A plain `julia --project=docs docs/make.jl` there used to print `makedocs: SKIPPED` and exit 0. gate_problems now reports [:open, :committed], so gate_or_skip calls check(...,1), which throws `gbg gate check-docs check-consistency returned 1`, and the build goes red. That is the ordinary mid-round state of every docs round, not an edge case. Only local builds are affected: in CI `in_ci` suppresses :committed, and `gbg round build` sets GBG_ROUND, which skips the round before either kind is pushed. The session's pre-commit docs build during a round, which CLAUDE.md requires, now fails where it used to skip. That brings back, locally, the "a red run that means a round is open" the skip was introduced to remove.
findings.title: The docs-build skip now also fails on a :committed refusal, which is wider than the disabled-instrument defect it fixed

findings.description: The defect the round names (ext#4, per the test comment 'beside an open round of a disabled instrument the build fails') is the disabled-instrument case, and the only new test covers that case alone. The fix goes wider: it also ends the skip for :committed, a signal that at build time cannot tell 'fixes committed without the round' from 'round files not committed yet'. The commit message says the :committed exclusion is intended. Even so, it converts a known over-approximation of the gate, which the skip used to absorb, into a hard failure of the local docs build, and no test checks it.
findings.before:
docs_build_skipped(cfg::AbstractDict, code::Integer) =
    code == 1 && !haskey(ENV, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP") ? frozen_rounds(cfg, "check-docs", "check-consistency") : String[]
findings.why_it_matters: The concrete input is a local (no CI variable) `julia --project=docs docs/make.jl` with GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP unset, during an open check-docs or check-consistency round, after at least one commit since the round opened (ROUND.head is the HEAD at open, so the round-opening commit is already one), while any file under the round directory is untracked or modified. Git.porcelain counts untracked files by default, so lane findings/*.json not yet committed or a pass's verdicts/pass-k files are enough. At base that build printed `makedocs: SKIPPED` and returned `nothing`, exit 0. Now gate_problems adds a :committed problem beside the :open one, the skip is refused, and check() throws `gbg gate check-docs check-consistency returned 1`. That state is the normal one for most of a round, and it does not yet mean the fixes were committed without the round, because the round files are simply not committed yet. A session that follows CLAUDE.md's 'gate every commit on exit codes' with the bare docs build mid-round used to get exit 0 and now gets a failure. Mitigation: both PROTOCOL.md files send a mid-round build through `gbg round build`, which sets GBG_ROUND, makes the gate skip the round and so avoids both :open and :committed. check-consistency's protocol even says a bare make.jl under an open round 'is refused by the gate, by design'. The usage that is newly rejected was therefore already off-protocol, but it was previously an exit-0 no-op.
findings.title: A bare local docs build during an open docs round now throws whenever the round's files are uncommitted after HEAD moved, where it used to skip with exit 0
findings.evidence: Gate.jl (unchanged logic): `if !in_ci && head !== nothing && head != r.round["head"] ... any(p -> startswith(p, rel * "/") || p == rel, dirty) && push!(problems, :committed => ...)`, with `dirty = Set(p for (_, p) in Git.porcelain(root))` and Git.jl `Git.porcelain(root; untracked = true)`. Preflight.jl:723 records `"head" => head` at open. test/gate.jl adds only `@test Set(first.(last(G.gate_problems(off, ...)))) == Set([:open, :disabled])` and `@test isempty(G.docs_build_skipped(off, 1))`, and no :committed case. The DocLints docstring now says: 'A refusal that also names an open round of a disabled instrument, or a round whose fixes were committed without it, fails the build.'

findings.description: The exit-1 skip/fail split for makedocs() moved from being keyed purely on the gate's return code to being keyed on the KIND of every problem the gate found; a mixed refusal (open docs round + a disabled-instrument round, or + an uncommitted-round problem) that used to be swallowed as a skip is now a build failure. This is the one behavioural change in an otherwise docstring-only diff, and it is well-tested and well-documented, but it is exactly the shape the lane watches for: a previously-working input (from makedocs' caller's point of view) now takes a different path.
findings.before:
docs_build_skipped(cfg::AbstractDict, code::Integer) =
    code == 1 && !haskey(ENV, "GBG_DOCS_NO_SKIP") ? frozen_rounds(cfg, "check-docs", "check-consistency") : String[]
findings.why_it_matters: makedocs() (via ext/GBGCodingToolsDocumenterExt.jl's gate_or_skip) calls this to decide whether an exit-1 gate refusal is a benign skip (build exits 0) or a real failure. Before this diff, ANY exit-1 refusal while a docs round was open was treated as a skip, regardless of what else the gate objected to. After this diff, a refusal is only a skip when every problem the gate lists is :open; if a :disabled-instrument round or a :committed-without-the-round problem is ALSO present, the same gate exit code 1 now falls through to check(), which throws and fails the docs build. A consumer with a stray open round of a disabled instrument sitting alongside a normal frozen docs round — an input that previously built green with a skip line — now gets a hard build failure. The change is deliberate, documented in the updated docstring, and pinned by a new test/gate.jl case (ext#4 of 2026-09-11-check-docs-02; the skip used to swallow it), and the WORK_QUEUE shows it closing an already-known defect from a prior audit round, so it is a corrected contract rather than an unannounced one — but it is still a case where previously-valid input's outcome (skip, exit 0) changed to a different outcome (build failure) for the same gate exit code.
findings.title: docs_build_skipped() now fails a build it used to silently skip
findings.evidence: test/gate.jl: "@test isempty(G.docs_build_skipped(off, 1))  # the second refusal fails the build" and the comment "a refusal the open docs round does not explain ALONE is never a skip ... the skip used to swallow it"

findings.description: This is a documentation-only change (no code or schema in the diff touches the four closure channels, Demote.jl's predicate, or any schema file), so it does not itself alter behavior for any previously-valid input. It is reported because it is the one place in the diff that brushes up against the §5.5 closed-vocabulary invariant: it introduces new terminology ("the fifth channel") for a mechanism that the design's own §6.5 heading defines as never closing, inside the exact module docstring that is supposed to be the map of the four-channel closed set.
findings.after: the demotion and the four closure channels — `honored`, `adjudicated`, `seeded` and `rescan` — and writes the tally; [`Passes.close`](@ref) checks every closing condition of the instrument ([`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds the term) in order, carries what a spent pass budget left open (the fifth channel, `carried`) and stamps the round closed.
findings.before: the demotion and the four closure channels and writes the tally; [`Passes.close`](@ref) checks every closing condition of the instrument ([`GBGCodingTools`](@ref) binds the term) in order and stamps the round closed.
findings.why_it_matters: §5.5 lists "the closure predicates and the four channels" as a closed vocabulary whose size is deliberately fixed and MAJOR to change, and ARCHITECTURE §6.5 titles the concept "Closure channels (per finding id; PARTIAL never closes)" — a channel is specifically something that CLOSES a finding id. `carried` is the opposite: a carried id is explicitly left OPEN across rounds. No code, schema, or RULES.toml changed in this diff — the four real closure channels and the schema they validate against are untouched — but the docstring now hands a future reader (or a future doc-consistency scan) the label "the fifth channel" for a mechanism the design elsewhere insists never closes anything, which is exactly the kind of prose drift that could later be cited to justify treating `carried` as a fifth entry in the closed vocabulary without the MAJOR bump §5.5 requires.
